podcast.body: Travis frequented The Good Mixer pub on Inverness Street in Camden, London, becoming regulars after the initial Britpop surge in the early and mid-1990s. The pub was a notable social hub for bands and artists during this period. "Other regulars included the Librieteens and then later the darkness and travis."

xref.title: Formation as a Supergroup (2003)
xref.body: Formed in 2003, Velvet Revolver began with former Guns N' Roses members Duff McKagan, Slash, and Matt Sorum, who then recruited Dave Kushner from Wasted Youth. They auditioned several singers, including Josh Todd of Buckcherry, Travis Meeks of Days of the New, and B-Real of Cypress Hill, before settling on Scott Weiland. "Susan told Mary that three guys from Guns and Roses had kissed and made up and were forming a new band."

"The guys had already tried out...Travis Meeks of days that the new and neither them worked out."

xref.title: Estrangement from Blink 182 (2005-2022)
xref.body: Following Blink 182's indefinite hiatus in 2005, Tom DeLonge and Mark Hoppus did not communicate for years. He notably quit Blink 182 twice, the second time in early 2015, either to focus on non-musical projects or due to an unwillingness to sign a contract requiring sole focus on the band. He remained estranged from Mark and Travis through 2021. "Tom DeLong and bass player Mark Hoppiz did not talk for years."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Formation During Blink 182 Hiatus (Post-2005)
xref.body: This band was formed by Mark Hoppus and Travis Barker during Blink 182's indefinite hiatus, a period when Mark Hoppus and Tom DeLonge were not speaking. It was one of several solo/side projects that emerged during that time. "Bands like Tom's Angels and Airwaves and Mark and Travis's Plus 44."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Indefinite Hiatus and Breakup (2005)
xref.body: Over Christmas 2004, old tensions resurfaced, leading to a breakdown in communication among band members. On February 22, 2005, management announced an "indefinite hiatus." The statement explained the band's need for time with loved ones after over a decade of non-stop work. However, this was effectively a breakup, initiated when Tom DeLonge's demand for a six-month break was deemed too long by Mark and Travis, leading to Tom quitting the band. "On February 22, 2005, announcing that the group was going on, quote, indefinite hiatus."

xref.title: 2008 Plane Crash and Tattoo Impact
xref.body: In 2008, Travis Barker was a survivor of a severe plane crash, which resulted in third-degree burns across his body. The subsequent skin graft procedures led to the loss of a significant portion of his existing tattoos, requiring new ink to be applied to the healed skin. "Travis, he's the survivor of a terrible plane crash back in 2008 that left him with third-degree burns all over his body. That's, and the subsequent skin grafts wiped out a lot of his ink. So once he healed, the new skin got new ink."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Blink-182 Reunion Catalyst (2008)
xref.body: The only positive outcome of Travis Barker's near-fatal plane crash, beyond his survival, was that it spurred the reunion of Blink-182. The band later released the album "Neighborhoods" almost exactly three years after the incident. "About the only good thing about the whole incident, other than the fact that Travis lived, is that it spurred the reunion of Blink 182."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Crash Cause and Injuries (2008)
xref.body: The Learjet crash that Travis Barker survived on September 19, 2008, was attributed to badly underinflated tires that burst during acceleration, leading the pilot to abort takeoff at too high a speed, resulting in a loss of control. Travis suffered severe physical and mental scars, spending nearly three months in hospitals and burn units, undergoing 16 surgeries, and facing a potential foot amputation, alongside severe PTSD. "Well, the tires of the jet were badly underinflated, which caused them to burst as the plane gathered speed."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Fatal Plane Crash (2008)
xref.body: DJ A.M. was one of two survivors, along with Travis Barker, of a catastrophic Learjet 60 plane crash on September 19, 2008, in Columbia, South Carolina. He had convinced Travis Barker to take the chartered private jet after a show. "Travis and AM were the only two people to survive."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 3

xref.title: Hospital Reunion (2008)
xref.body: Following Travis Barker's severe injuries from the plane crash, Mark Hoppus was among the first to visit him in the hospital, and Tom Delonge also made the trip. The three members of Blink-182 met in a "sobering reunion" at Travis's bedside, prompting a realization for all three about what truly mattered in their lives and relationships. "The three guys met up in the hospital in a pretty sobering reunion."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 3

xref.title: Jerry Finn's Death (2008)
xref.body: The sudden death of their long-time producer Jerry Finn in 2008, coupled with Travis Barker's near-fatal plane crash, "shocked everyone back to reality" and helped the band members sort out their issues, leading to their eventual reunion. "along with drummer Travis Barker's near fatal plane crash and the sudden death of their long-time producer Jerry Flynn, both in 2008. That shocked everyone back to reality and things got sorted out."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Learjet Crash Survival (2008)
xref.body: On September 19, 2008, Travis Barker survived a Learjet 60 crash in Columbia, South Carolina, after performing with one of his side projects. His wife, who was supposed to join him, had a "freaky feeling" and stayed behind. The plane failed to lift off, hit runway lights, crashed through a fence, crossed a highway, and ended against an embankment, killing four of the six people onboard, including the two pilots. Travis and DJ AM survived with severe burns. "Something went very wrong on takeoff. Even though the weather was fine, the plane failed to lift off by the time it reached the end of the runway."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Learjet Crash Survival and Recovery (2008)
xref.body: On September 19, 2008, after a performance in Columbia, South Carolina, Travis Barker boarded a Learjet 60 bound for Van Nuys, California. His wife, sensing a premonition, stayed behind. During takeoff, the plane failed to lift off, hitting runway lights, crashing through a fence, crossing a highway, and ultimately striking an embankment. Four of the six occupants, including both pilots, died. Travis and DJ AM survived but sustained severe burns. The crash was attributed to badly underinflated tires bursting, leading the pilot to abort takeoff at an unsafe speed. Travis endured 16 surgeries over nearly three months, faced potential foot amputation, and suffered severe PTSD. "It was touching go for Travis for a very long time. He was in and out of hospitals and burn units for nearly three months."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Learjet Crash Survival and Subsequent Death (2008-2009)
xref.body: DJ AM survived the September 19, 2008, Learjet 60 crash with Travis Barker, suffering second and third-degree burns, and was released from the hospital weeks before Barker. However, less than a year later, he was found dead in his New York apartment from a drug overdose, a poly-substance intoxication involving crack, cocaine, oxycodone, and other drugs. "DJ Am also had second and third degree burns, although he was released from hospital weeks before Travis. But less than a year later, he was found dead in his apartment in New York. A drug overdose. Crack, cocaine, oxy, and a ton of other stuff."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Near-Fatal Plane Crash and Fear of Flying (2008)
xref.body: Travis Barker was involved in a near-fatal plane crash in 2008, an event that, alongside producer Jerry Finn's death, "shocked everyone back to reality" and helped resolve internal band issues. The crash left him with a lasting fear of flying, which subsequently made it impossible for him to tour with Blink 182 overseas. "along with drummer Travis Barker's near fatal plane crash and the sudden death of their long-time producer Jerry Flynn, both in 2008. That shocked everyone back to reality and things got sorted out."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Plane Crash Injuries and Recovery (2008)
xref.body: Travis Barker sustained severe injuries in the September 2008 Learjet crash, suffering 30 re-burns to 65% of his body and developing blood clots. He spent four months in a Georgia hospital, undergoing 27 different surgeries. Amputation was considered, but he underwent tangential excision (scraping away dead skin). The agony was so intense that he offered friends a million dollars to end his suffering. He also developed PTSD and eventually divorced his wife after the ordeal. "Travis had 30 re-burns to 65% of his body. He had blood clots all over. He was in a Georgia hospital for four months and had 27 different surgeries."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 3

xref.title: Reunion Triggered by Plane Crash (2008)
xref.body: One of the positive outcomes of drummer Travis Barker's near-fatal plane crash on September 19, 2008, was that it served as a catalyst for the reunion of Blink-182. The band subsequently released the album "Neighborhoods" almost three years to the day after the crash. "About the only good thing about the whole incident, other than the fact that Travis lived, is that it spurred the reunion of Blink 182."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Travis Barker's Plane Crash (2008)
xref.body: On September 19, 2008, less than a month after Jerry Finn's death, Travis Barker and DJ AM were involved in a Learjet 60 plane crash in Columbia, South Carolina, after a show. The chartered plane, which Travis was persuaded to take by DJ AM, suffered underinflated tires that burst during takeoff, causing the landing gear to collapse and the plane to crash through lights, a fence, across a highway, and into an embankment. Travis and DJ AM were the only two survivors from the six people on board. "Then came the plane crash. This was September 19th, 2008."

xref.title: Resurfacing Internal Issues (Late 2014)
xref.body: After their album *Dogs Eating Dogs* and more tours, the "old cracks returned" within the band. Issues between Tom DeLonge and Mark Hoppus, coupled with Travis Barker's fear of flying preventing overseas tours, came to a head in late 2014. "There were more tours, but the old cracks returned."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Tom DeLonge's Departures (2014-2015)
xref.body: Tom DeLonge initially quit the band for one day in early 2014 but was persuaded to return. Tensions escalated again in early 2015 when he insisted on recording his parts in San Diego while Mark and Travis worked in LA. A week before studio convergence, Mark and Travis received an email from Tom's manager stating his unwillingness to participate, citing a desire to focus on non-musical projects. Another account suggests he was presented with a 60-page contract demanding sole focus on Blink, which he couldn't accept due to prior commitments. He consequently quit for a second time. "Tensions built, and a week before everyone was supposed to convene in the studio for the final push, Mark and Travis got an email from Tom's manager saying that he no longer wanted to participate in Blink 182."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Matt Skiba's Recruitment and First Performance (2015)
xref.body: After Tom DeLonge's second departure, Mark Hoppus and Travis Barker decided against disbanding Blink 182 and recruited Matt Skiba from Alkaline Trio. Their first performance with Skiba on March 18, 2015, marked the first time Mark Hoppus played in Blink without Tom DeLonge, after which Skiba was made an official member. "Mark and Travis had no plans to kill Blink so they brought in Matt Skiba from Alkaline Trio."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Personal Life Developments (Post-2015)
xref.body: During this period, Travis Barker's personal life saw significant changes; he got divorced, became involved with the Kardashians, and made more TV appearances. He was also involved in a car accident where his SUV collided with a school bus, though he was not injured. "He got divorced, got wrapped up with a Kardashians, appeared on more TV shows, and got into a bad car accident, whereas SUV collided with a school bus."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Prolific Collaborator and Producer (2015-2022)
xref.body: Over a seven-year period, Travis Barker became a highly active collaborator and producer, appearing on numerous records. His extensive list of collaborations includes artists such as Young Blood, The Game, M&M, Stevie O'Kee, LL Cool J, Pitbull, Lights, Kenny Hoopla, Machine Gun Kelly, Halsey, Willow Smith, and Dirty Heads. "Travis Barker seemed willing to collaborate and produce just about anyone, and he would appear in a ton of records over the next seven years."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Replaced Tom DeLonge in Blink 182 (2015)
xref.body: In March 2015, Matt Skiba was brought in from Alkaline Trio to replace Tom DeLonge in Blink 182. After performing three initial gigs, starting March 18, 2015, he was made an official member of the band. "Mark and Travis had no plans to kill Blink so they brought in Matt Skiba from Alkaline Trio."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Struggle with Depression and Anger (2018-2019)
xref.body: During the period leading up to and during the recording of Blink 182's *Nine* album, Mark Hoppus struggled severely with depression. His wife encouraged him to pursue activities that brought him happiness, leading to the formation of Simple Creatures in 2018. His lyrics for *Nine* were notably darker, reflecting his internal battles, his anger over mass shootings (particularly one near Travis Barker's home), and his frustration with Donald Trump's policies. He was also not sober at this time. "But hold up though, Mark was struggling with depression during this time. And it was bad."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Hip-Hop Influence on "Nine" (2019)
xref.body: Travis Barker's strong interest in hip-hop heavily influenced the rhythms he created for many of the 15 songs on Blink 182's *Nine* album. This rhythmic foundation, combined with the incorporation of loops and electronics, contributed a "different sort of flavor" to the band's sound. "Nine features 15 songs, most of which seem to have been constructed around rhythms created by Travis, which since Travis was so big into hip-hop, gave the album a different sort of flavor."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
The Ongoing History of New Music
The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Astroworld Festival Deaths (November 5, 2021)
xref.body: During Travis Scott's performance at the Astroworld Festival in Houston on November 5, 2021, ten people died—eight on-site and two later in the hospital—all from compressive asphyxiation, with victims aged 14 to 27. At least 300 additional people were injured in a severe crowd-crush incident attributed to a gross failure of crowd control, crowd safety, and security. "Ten people died during Travis Scott's sad during the Asterole Festival on November 5th, 2021."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Reconciliation with Mark Hoppus and Travis Barker (2022)
xref.body: Upon learning of Mark Hoppus's cancer diagnosis, Tom DeLonge immediately reached out, leading to a crucial meeting in Mark's backyard that included Travis Barker. During this sit-down, they discussed life experiences, growth, and the realization that personal issues paled in comparison to Mark's health. This meeting was pivotal in healing damaged relationships and ultimately facilitated Tom's return to Blink 182. "When Tom's long heard about Mark, he was right there and soon there was a sit down in Mark's backyard."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Tom DeLonge's Return and Reconciliation (2022)
xref.body: By mid-2022, rumors of a reunion circulated, leading to the band's social media accounts being wiped in October. On October 11, the official announcement was made that Tom DeLonge was back, and an album and a two-year world tour were planned. This reconciliation was spurred by Mark Hoppus's cancer diagnosis, which prompted Tom to reach out immediately. "And that's when news came down that Mark, Travis and Tom, came to the realization that it was time to bury all the animosities and get back to being Blink 182."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Coachella Comeback Performance (2023)
xref.body: On April 14, 2023, Blink 182 was announced as a surprise replacement headliner for Frank Ocean at Coachella with only two days' notice. This marked the original lineup's (Mark, Travis, Tom) first performance together in nine years (since 2014). They played an hour-long set to an audience of 150,000, which was described as one big sing-along. "In the interim, they got to make a big comeback together at Coachella on April 14th, 2023."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Producer of "One More Time" (2023)
xref.body: Travis Barker took on the role of producer for Blink 182's *One More Time* album, with most of the recording conducted at his home studio. While initially a sensitive and unplanned arrangement, it became evident as sessions progressed that he was "up to the task." "There was no outside producer. Travis Barker handled all that and most of the recording was done at his home studio."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.body: For their self-titled 2003 album, the band sought to grow beyond "goofy adolescent" songs. Influenced by their side projects, Tom and Travis brought a new attitude to Blink 182, resulting in a more experimental, darker, and mature sound. "Like all musicians, they wanted to grow."

xref.title: Extensive Legal Actions and Industry Impact
xref.body: The Astroworld disaster has initiated a protracted investigation and over 3,000 lawsuits that will take a considerable amount of time to resolve. The incident has prompted promoters globally to re-evaluate and modify their festival policing and security protocols, underscoring the substantial financial consequences for entities like Live Nation and Travis Scott. "The investigation into this one will take a very long time and it'll take forever to sort out the more than 3,000 lawsuits that have been filed."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Extensive Tattoo Coverage
xref.body: Travis Barker is noted for having an exceptionally high number of tattoos, with the last count distinguishing 117 different and distinct tattoos. These cover his body from the top of his head down to his toes, with more than 70% of his body covered. "He's right from the top of his head all the way down to his toes. In fact, more than 70% of the man's body is covered with tattoos."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Family Tattoos
xref.body: Travis has the names of his children, Alabama and London, tattooed on his body. Additionally, a skull tattoo covers the name of his ex-wife, Shanna Mokler, which was previously on his body. "His children's names are there. That's Alabama and London."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Fashion Company
xref.body: Travis Barker ventured into the fashion industry by establishing his own company, Famous Stars and Strapz. The brand specialized in selling t-shirts, shoes, and various types of skate gear, reflecting his personal style and interests. "Travis got into fashion, starting up a company called Famous Stars and Strapz, a self-t shirts and shoes and all kinds of skate gear."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 3

xref.title: Fired from Blink-182
xref.body: In May 1998, despite agreeing to enter rehab, Tom DeLong and Mark Hoppas felt that Scott's behavior was negatively impacting the band's performances, leading to his dismissal. While some accounts suggest he was fired over the phone, he was ultimately replaced by Travis Barker. "So Scott was fired. Some story said he was fired over the phone, but whatever the case is, he was out and Travis was in."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 1

xref.title: Five-Year Silence with Tom DeLonge
xref.body: By mid-2008, a significant communication breakdown had occurred between Travis Barker and Tom DeLonge, with Travis noting that he hadn't spoken a word to Tom in five years. This extended silence highlighted the deep rifts within Blink-182, making the prospect of a reunion seem unlikely. "Travis hadn't said a word to Tom in five years or would be the point of getting back together of nobody's talking."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 3

xref.title: Formation and Origin of Name
xref.body: Plus 44 was formed by Mark Hoppus and Travis Barker during Blink-182's hiatus, initially conceived as a more electronic project. The band's name, "Plus 44," was inspired by the international dialing code for the United Kingdom, where the idea for the band first germinated among its members. "Mark Hoppiss and Travis Barker formed a band that they called Plus 44. That name comes from the code you have to use to call the UK."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 3

xref.title: Formation and Sound
xref.body: This group originated with Tim Armstrong, who was experimenting with computer-generated hip-hop beats. Travis Barker joined as the final piece of the band, allowing him to explore more demanding drumming parts than he typically played with Blink 182. It's described as an indie punk supergroup. "Travis had his own muses to follow. He and Tim Armstrong from Ranset got together to explore hip-hop beats in a group called the Transplants."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 2

xref.title: Formation by Mark and Travis (Post-Blink 182)
xref.body: Mark and Travis formed this new band after Blink 182 split, and it "did okay." "Well, Mark and Travis stuck together in a new band they called Plus 44, which also did okay."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Reunions: Some Lasted....and Sadly, Some Didn't ｜ Part 1

xref.title: Former Calabasas Mansion
xref.body: John Mayer's old mansion in Calabasas, a gated community in California also home to Will Smith, Justin Bieber, and Travis Barker, was used as a studio where USS co-wrote the song "Who's With Me" with a member of OneRepublic. "We wrote it with a guy that was in one republic and when I we he lived in John Mayor's old mansion."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: USS In Their Own Words: Part 2

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About The Smiths

xref.title: Genre Exploration
xref.body: Willow has explored several different styles and genres throughout her musical career, ultimately finding a particular talent and comfort in punk pop. "She's gone through several different styles in genres. But really seems to have a flair for punk pop, working on her own as well as collaborating with people like Machine Gun Kelly and Travis Barker of Blink 182."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Hip-Hop Collaborations
xref.body: Musically, Travis Barker delved deeper into beat-making and rhythm, collaborating with a range of hip-hop artists on both recording sessions and remixes. This expanded his musical repertoire beyond rock drumming. "And musically he got deeper into beats, working with a series of hip-hop artists on recording and remixes."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 3

xref.title: Jerry Finn's Push for Other Projects
xref.body: Longtime producer Jerry Finn, along with Mark Hoppus and Travis Barker, made it clear they wanted to work on another project during Blink-182's hiatus. This desire led to the formation of Plus 44 by Mark and Travis, further solidifying the band's fragmentation. "It also didn't help the situation that the other two thirds of the band and their long time producer Jerry Finn made it very clear that they wanted to work together on another project."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 3

xref.title: Joining The Aquabats
xref.body: Travis Barker joined The Aquabats in 1997, a period during which he was working as a trash collector and welcomed the opportunity to play in a band. "Travis joined the band in 1997. He was working as a trash collector and was grateful for a chance to play in a band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 1

xref.title: Learning Blink-182 Songs Quickly
xref.body: According to legend, Travis Barker impressively learned the drum parts for 20 Blink-182 songs in just 45 minutes when he was asked to temporarily fill in for Scott Rainer. "Legend says that he learned his parts to 20 Blink 182 songs in 45 minutes. That's pretty impressive."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 1

xref.title: Lending Travis Barker to Blink
xref.body: The Aquabats displayed remarkable cooperation by "really cool"ly lending their drummer, Travis Barker, to Blink when Scott Rainer needed to return to California. "When Scott Rainer had to go back to California, the Aquabats were really cool in lending Travis to Blink."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 1

xref.title: Live DJing and Drumming Project
xref.body: DJ A.M. collaborated with Travis Barker on a unique musical project that blended live drums with DJ mixing. DJ A.M. would spin classic songs on his turntables, while Travis Barker augmented the grooves with live drumming, creating an innovative performance style that they shared online. "Their idea was to combine a DJ's mixing with live drums. DJ A.M. would spin classic songs and his decks and Travis would augment the groove."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 3

xref.title: Mark Hoppus's Isolation During Side Projects
xref.body: While Tom DeLonge and Travis Barker pursued side projects like Box Car Racer and The Transplants, Mark Hoppus "stayed on the sidelines quietly fuming," feeling betrayed that Tom had asked Travis to drum for Box Car Racer, a project that had an "old DIY vibe of early Blink." "Mark left the studio and wrote what he thought would be an instant rejection."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 2

xref.title: Musical Dedication After Mother's Death
xref.body: Following the death of his mother when he was 15, Travis intensely focused on music, taking numerous lessons, including from a jazz teacher, and dedicated hours to studying funk rhythms and practicing rudiments, leading to his exceptional drumming skills. "When his mother died, when he was 15, he threw himself into music. He took a lot of lessons, including plenty from a jazz teacher."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 1

xref.title: Name Origin
xref.body: The name "Box Car Racer" was shared with a previous band Travis Barker was in before Blink 182. The common story that it alluded to the B-52 bomber that dropped the atomic bomb on Nagasaki is incorrect; its true origin is Travis's old band. "The real origin goes back to Travis's old band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 2

xref.title: Performance Continued Amidst Tragedy
xref.body: Despite the unfolding fatal crowd-crush situation and significant injuries during his Astroworld Festival set, Travis Scott continued his performance for over an hour. "And while this was happening, Travis Scott continued with his set for over an hour."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Pioneer of Exaggerated Auto-Tune Use
xref.body: Kanye is recognized as one of the artists who "really went to town with auto-tune," utilizing the technology not just for subtle pitch correction but for highly exaggerated and distinct vocal effects. His influential work contributed significantly to the trend of Auto-Tune being used as a deliberate stylistic choice in popular music. "Kanye, T-Pain, Travis Scott, and many others really went to town with auto-tune."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 5: (60-51)

xref.title: Pioneer of Exaggerated Auto-Tune Use
xref.body: T-Pain is cited as an artist who "really went to town with auto-tune," employing the software for pronounced, stylistic vocal effects that extended beyond simple pitch correction. His widespread and distinctive use of Auto-Tune played a crucial role in popularizing its exaggerated application in mainstream music. "Kanye, T-Pain, Travis Scott, and many others really went to town with auto-tune."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 5: (60-51)

xref.title: Pioneer of Exaggerated Auto-Tune Use
xref.body: Travis Scott is listed among the artists who "really went to town with auto-tune," leveraging the technology to create highly exaggerated and unique vocal sounds. His work exemplifies the trend of using Auto-Tune as a creative effect rather than solely for pitch correction, shaping its perception in contemporary music. "Kanye, T-Pain, Travis Scott, and many others really went to town with auto-tune."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 5: (60-51)

xref.title: Plus 44 Tour Experience
xref.body: The tour supporting the album "When Your Heart Stop's Beating" was a highlight for Mark Hoppus and Travis Barker (members of Plus 44), providing them the opportunity to play small clubs again after a long time, which was a re-energizing experience. During this tour, Travis Barker broke his arm during a video shoot, causing him immense pain and forcing him to miss several gigs. "The best part about it was the tour where Mark and Tom got to play small clubs for the first time in a long time. That was really energizing."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 3

xref.title: Pre-Crash Premonition and Message
xref.body: On the way to the airport for a chartered Learjet 60 flight with DJ AM, Travis Barker had a strong premonition that something was amiss. He consumed several joints, three Vicodin, and his Xanax. Before boarding, he sent a picture of the small plane to a friend with a message expressing his unease and detailing his wishes for his children if anything were to happen to him. "Travis had a bad feeling on the way to the airport... I'm just letting you know, something doesn't feel right. The plane is really small. If anything happens to me, make sure the kids get the house and they're taken care of."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 3

xref.title: Procis/Field Day Band Tattoo
xref.body: Travis Barker has a tattoo of the band Procis on his chest, which is the previous name for the band Field Day. This indicates his deep connection to the band's history. "He's got a tattoo. Can I say a process chest, which is this band. They're now called Field Day."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Reality TV Show
xref.body: Travis Barker starred in a reality television series called "Meet the Barkers" on MTV. The show documented his life with his wife, Shannon Mochler, even extending to filming inside the Blink-182 rehearsal space, which was a point of contention for Tom DeLonge. "Remember, meet the Barkers? That was an MTV show that followed Travis and his wife Shannon Mochler everywhere, including into the Blink rehearsal space."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 3

xref.title: Steve-O's Support for Famous Stars and Straps
xref.body: Steve-O of Sum 41 is mentioned as someone who publicly wears gear from Travis Barker's clothing company, Famous Stars and Straps, contributing to the brand's visibility. This highlights collaboration and mutual support among artists in their non-musical endeavors. "and Steve O of some 41".

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Temporary Role Before Full Membership
xref.body: When Blink-182 began recording "Enema of the State," Travis was initially brought in as a hired musician rather than a full-time member, before eventually transitioning into a permanent role with the band. "Not necessarily as a full-time member, but as a hired musician."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 1

xref.title: The Good Mixer Regulars
xref.body: The Libertines were among the bands who were regular patrons of The Good Mixer pub on Inverness Street in Camden, London, during the Britpop era of the early and mid-1990s. This pub was a key social spot where many groups of the era would gather. "Other regulars included the Librieteens and then later the darkness and travis."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Alt Rock Shrines ｜ From the Archives

xref.title: The Good Mixer Regulars
xref.body: The Darkness were noted as regular attendees of The Good Mixer pub on Inverness Street in Camden, London, following the initial Britpop wave in the early and mid-1990s. This pub was a central meeting point for musicians of the era. "Other regulars included the Librieteens and then later the darkness and travis."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Alt Rock Shrines ｜ From the Archives

xref.title: The Modern Age EP and Bidding War
xref.body: The Strokes recorded a three-track demo in 2000, which was unusually tight for a young group due to their insistence on rehearsing to a click track. This led to "The Modern Age" EP, which sold well and ignited one of the fiercest bidding wars among record labels in a long time. Rough Trade Records (UK) won the bid, prompting label head Geoff Travis to resurrect the label to sign The Strokes. They also secured a deal with RCA, which was amenable to the band's desire to make a music video. "The subsequent EP, the three track, the modern age, not only sold respectively well, but also sparked a bidding war amongst record labels."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Tim Armstrong's Support for Famous Stars and Straps
xref.body: Tim Armstrong of Rancid is noted for publicly wearing gear from Travis Barker's clothing company, Famous Stars and Straps, helping to promote the brand. This shows support among musicians for each other's entrepreneurial ventures. "If you look carefully, you can see Travis's gear on you guys like Tim Armstrong of Ransid".

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Tom Delonge's Desire for Break
xref.body: Tom Delonge's decision to take a break stemmed from feeling the intense grind of the band's schedule and needing at least six months to decompress. He was disappointed that Mark Hoppus and Travis Barker didn't fully understand his need for this extended time away. "The story seems to be that Tom just wanted a break from the grind and he was disappointed that the other two guys didn't understand why he needed at least six months to decompress."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 3

xref.title: Travis Barker Production
xref.body: Travis Barker of Blink-182 has produced some of Ho99o9's songs, indicating the band's cross-genre appeal and production quality. "And Travis Barker of Blink 182 is produced some of their songs."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 3: The New Genres

xref.title: Travis Barker's Accessory Companies
xref.body: Travis Barker, the drummer for Blink-182, has established himself in the fashion accessory market. He owns a belt buckle company named American Dream and a shoe company known as DC Shoes, showcasing his involvement in the business side of youth culture fashion. "Travis Barker of Blink 182 has a hot belt buckle company called American Dream and a shoe company called DC Shoes."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Travis Barker's Artistic Stretch
xref.body: Travis Barker appreciated the opportunity to stretch himself musically with The Transplants, learning to play drum parts that were significantly more demanding than those required in Blink 182. "Travis Barker from Blink 182, who really love the idea of being able to stretch himself by learning to play parts that were much more demanding than what he was called on to do with Blink 182."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 2

xref.title: Travis Barker's Band
xref.body: Travis Barker, who has collaborated with KennyHoopla, is a member of Blink-182. "Travis Barker of Blink, when it II."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Travis Barker's Cadillac Obsession
xref.body: Travis Barker, the drummer for Blink-182, demonstrates a profound love for Cadillacs, evidenced by numerous tattoos and a substantial car collection. His tattoos include a Chevrolet emblem on his left hand, the 1947 Cadillac logo over his heart, a similar emblem and the cursive "Cadillac" font on his right torso, a 1953 Cadillac on his back, and crossed racing flags with "66" (the year of his favorite Cadillac) on his neck. His multi-million dollar car collection features several Cadillacs, including a 1965 Deville convertible, a 1960 Coupe Deville, and a 1941 Series 62 Deluxe. "Travis has millions of dollars worth of cars, which includes several Caddies, including a 1965 Deville convertible."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Travis Barker's Clothing Company – Famous Stars and Straps
xref.body: Travis Barker, drummer for blink-182, founded the clothing company Famous Stars and Straps in 1999, based in Corona, California. The brand targets the skate crowd and offers t-shirts, jackets, and hats for men, along with shirts, pants, and bikinis for women, in addition to accessories like belt buckles and bandanas. The company's success is bolstered by famous friends, including Tim Armstrong of Rancid, Steve-O of Sum 41, members of Avenged Sevenfold, and B-Real of Cypress Hill, who wear the brand publicly. Famous Stars and Straps generates millions in annual revenue, and its presence is notable at events like the Warped Tour. "He founded the company in 1999 and targeted the Skate Crowd."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Travis Barker's Footwear and Headwear Lines for DC Shoes
xref.body: In addition to his own clothing company, Famous Stars and Straps, Travis Barker also designed a line of skate shoes and hats for DC Shoes. This demonstrates his entrepreneurial spirit beyond his role as a drummer. "And if that wasn't enough, Travis created a skate shoe and a line of hats for a company called DC Shoes."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Travis Barker's Involvement
xref.body: Travis Barker joined Tom DeLonge on drums for Box Car Racer, a decision that deeply upset Mark Hoppus of Blink 182, who felt betrayed. Travis only sang on a couple of tracks. "But then he asked Travis to be his drummer, which was okay for Travis, but it greatly pissed off Mark."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 2

xref.title: Tribute After Death
xref.body: Ozzy Osborne was among the many musicians who sent tributes upon Taylor Hawkins' death, underscoring the widespread respect and admiration he commanded from his peers. "When he died, tributes came in from everyone from Ozzy Osborne to Stevie Nicks, to Travis Barker, to Tom Morello to Liam Gallagher."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
